definition: protection or a sum of money given to someone against possible loss or damage

collocations.example: Workers can claim indemnity for injuries suffered on the job.
The bank issued a letter of indemnity to cover the shipment.

definition: made by a small, independent company rather than a large one

collocations.example: She starred in a low-budget indie film last year.
The indie band released its first album online.

definition: to teach someone to accept a set of beliefs without questioning them

collocations.example: Critics say the group tries to indoctrinate young people.
Teachers should educate children, not indoctrinate them with propaganda.

definition: not able to produce the result you want; weak and without effect

collocations.example: He was a well-meaning but ineffectual leader of the team.
All the rescue measures proved ineffectual in the end.

definition: showing no skill; very clumsy or awkward

collocations.example: He felt socially inept at large office parties.
She was utterly inept at handling the new software.

definition: to be filled with intense but short-lived love or admiration for someone

collocations.example: He was infatuated with the famous actress for months.
She soon became infatuated with her charming new colleague.

definition: physically weak, especially because of old age or illness

collocations.example: The charity cares for people who are old and infirm.
Nurses visited the infirm patients at home each week.

definition: a small hospital or a room where sick people are cared for

collocations.example: The sick student was sent to the school infirmary.
He spent two nights in the infirmary with a fever.

definition: to fix an idea or habit firmly in someone's mind

collocations.example: Coaches try to ingrain good habits in young players.
The custom is deeply ingrained in local culture.

definition: decorative material set into the surface of something to form a pattern

collocations.example: The table was decorated with delicate gold inlay.
The box was inlaid with mother-of-pearl.

definition: not harmful or offensive; completely harmless

collocations.example: It seemed a perfectly innocuous remark at the time.
The seemingly innocuous plant is actually poisonous.

definition: an indirect remark that hints at something rude or unpleasant

collocations.example: The song is full of sexual innuendo.
He attacked his opponent with a veiled innuendo.

definition: to protect someone against a disease by giving them a vaccine

collocations.example: The clinic will inoculate travelers against yellow fever.
A team of doctors came to inoculate the new recruits.

definition: much larger or greater than is reasonable; excessive

collocations.example: They spend an inordinate amount of time in meetings.
The project suffered from an inordinate delay.

definition: an official investigation held to find the cause of someone's death

collocations.example: The coroner will hold an inquest next week.
The inquest into his death opened yesterday in court.

definition: eager to learn or know about things; curious

collocations.example: She has a lively, inquisitive mind that loves new ideas.
The inquisitive child asked endless questions all day.

definition: a chemical substance used to kill insects

collocations.example: Farmers spray insecticide to protect their crops.
The field was treated with insecticide last month.

definition: a badge or sign that shows a person's rank, membership, or office

collocations.example: His uniform bore the insignia of a senior officer.
The heavy gates were marked with the royal insignia.

definition: to suggest something unpleasant in an indirect way

collocations.example: Are you trying to insinuate that I am lying?
He managed to insinuate doubts about her honesty.

definition: the condition of being regularly unable to sleep

collocations.example: She suffers from insomnia and rarely sleeps well.
Chronic insomnia left him exhausted every morning.

definition: a violent attempt by a group to take control of a government; a revolt

collocations.example: The rebels planned an armed insurrection against the king.
They tried to stage an insurrection when the talks failed.

definition: the educated, intellectual people in a society, viewed as a group

collocations.example: The reforms were supported by the liberal intelligentsia.
The local intelligentsia gathered to debate the issue.

definition: to interrupt a conversation by saying something suddenly

collocations.example: She paused to interject a quick comment of her own.
He interjected that the plan would never actually work.

definition: a short period of time between two events or parts of something

collocations.example: After a brief interlude of peace, the fighting resumed.
The play included a short musical interlude after act one.

definition: continuing for a very long time and therefore boring or annoying

collocations.example: We faced an interminable wait at the crowded airport.
The interminable meeting dragged on all afternoon.

definition: to place things at intervals among other things

collocations.example: She interspersed her speech with a few light jokes.
The editor interspersed photos among the long articles.

definition: to combine or twist things together closely

collocations.example: The novel interweaves a love story with a murder plot.
The author skillfully interweaves several themes in the book.

definition: the quality of having many small, complicated parts or details

collocations.example: The price depends on the intricacy of the design.
The carving was done with great intricacy and care.

definition: to treat something with radiation, often to kill bacteria or preserve it

collocations.example: Some companies irradiate food to kill harmful bacteria.
The spices are irradiated to extend their shelf life.

definition: unpleasantly surprising or not matching the surroundings

collocations.example: His cheerful tone struck a jarring note at the funeral.
There was a jarring contrast between the two design styles.

definition: a climbing plant with sweet-smelling white or yellow flowers

collocations.example: She enjoys a warm cup of jasmine tea in the evening.
The garden was filled with the scent of jasmine flowers.

definition: to laugh at or shout rudely at someone to show you have no respect

collocations.example: The crowd began to jeer at the losing team.
Spectators jeered loudly when the referee made the call.

definition: something said or done to be funny; a joke

collocations.example: The remark was made half in jest, not as an insult.
He said it in jest, but she took it seriously.

definition: a puzzle made of many small pieces that fit together to form a picture

collocations.example: The children spent the afternoon doing a jigsaw puzzle.
This new clue is the final piece of the jigsaw.

definition: a short, catchy song or tune used in advertising

collocations.example: The company created a catchy jingle for its new product.
Everyone still remembers the advertising jingle from that commercial.

definition: to shake or move in a quick, unsteady way

collocations.example: The worn old film made the picture jitter on the screen.
Her hands jittered nervously as she opened the letter.

definition: extremely large; much bigger than the usual size

collocations.example: The jumbo jet carried over four hundred passengers.
He ordered a jumbo size portion of fries.

definition: a particular point in time, especially an important or critical one

collocations.example: At this juncture, we must decide how to proceed.
The peace talks had reached a critical juncture.

definition: (informal) a person who is extremely enthusiastic about something

collocations.example: As an adrenaline junkie, he loves dangerous extreme sports.
She is a real news junkie and reads every headline.

definition: a military group that rules a country after taking power by force

collocations.example: A military junta seized control of the country overnight.
The ruling junta banned all public protests.

definition: a large Australian animal that moves by jumping on its strong back legs

collocations.example: A gray kangaroo bounded across the quiet country road.
The national park protects a large kangaroo population.

definition: the long piece of wood or steel along the bottom of a boat

collocations.example: The ship's keel scraped against the hidden rocks.
Workers laid the keel of the new vessel in January.

definition: an oven used for baking bricks or pottery at a high temperature

collocations.example: The bricks are left in the brick kiln to bake.
The potter fired the bowls in a very hot kiln.

definition: a unit of weight equal to 1,000 grams; a kilogram

collocations.example: She bought a kilo of apples at the market.
The fresh tomatoes cost two dollars per kilo.

definition: a unit of electrical power equal to 1,000 watts

collocations.example: Electricity in the city is billed by the kilowatt hour.
The heavy machine draws several kilowatts when running.

definition: a tight twist or bend in something long, such as a rope or wire

collocations.example: There was a kink in the garden hose, stopping the water.
She straightened out a kink in the tangled cable.

definition: a small oval fruit with brown skin and soft green flesh

collocations.example: The kiwi fruit is rich in vitamin C and tastes sweet.
I like to add a slice of kiwi to my breakfast.

definition: to press and stretch dough firmly with your hands

collocations.example: She began to knead the dough for the fresh bread.
Knead the mixture well until it becomes smooth and soft.

definition: a light, pale type of beer

collocations.example: He ordered a pint of lager at the busy pub.
They enjoyed a cold lager on the warm afternoon.

definition: the people of a religion who are not priests or members of the clergy

collocations.example: The new rules affect both the clergy and the laity.
The laity played a larger role in the church's events.

definition: a woman who rents out a room or property to tenants

collocations.example: My landlady raised the rent again this year.
The friendly pub landlady welcomed her regular customers.

definition: showing little energy or effort; slow and relaxed

collocations.example: He gave a languid gesture of farewell from the doorway.
They spent a languid afternoon by the quiet pool.

definition: to be forced to stay in an unpleasant situation for a long time

collocations.example: He continues to languish in prison without a trial.
The bill languished for years without a vote.

definition: the folded flap of cloth at the front of a jacket, below the collar

collocations.example: He wore a small red flower in his jacket lapel.
She fastened the name badge to her lapel.

definition: (of water) to move gently against something with a soft sound

collocations.example: The waves lapped against the side of the wooden boat.
Gentle water lapped at the children's bare feet.

definition: an evergreen tree or shrub with shiny leaves, used to make wreaths

collocations.example: The winner of the race was crowned with a laurel wreath.
A thick laurel bush grew beside the stone path.

definition: (of a substance) to be removed from soil or rock by water passing through it

collocations.example: Heavy rain can leach nutrients from the topsoil.
Chemicals slowly leach out of the buried waste.

definition: a long vegetable with white and green parts, related to the onion

collocations.example: She made a warm bowl of potato and leek soup.
He chopped a fresh leek finely for the stew.

definition: to look at someone in an unpleasant, often sexual way

collocations.example: He kept leering at the women across the crowded bar.
The stranger leered suggestively as she walked past.

definition: clear enough to be read easily

collocations.example: Her handwriting is neat and perfectly legible.
The old faded sign was barely legible in the dark.

definition: a feeling of having no energy and little interest in doing anything

collocations.example: A deep feeling of lethargy came over her that morning.
He was overcome by lethargy after the long flight.

definition: a small, flat plant-like growth that forms on rocks, walls, and trees

collocations.example: Gray lichen slowly covered the old stone wall.
A patch of lichen clung to the damp rock.

definition: something that provides essential help or support in a difficult time

collocations.example: The grant is a lifeline for struggling small farms.
The phone service provides a lifeline to elderly people living alone.

definition: a bush with sweet-smelling pale purple or white flowers

collocations.example: A lilac bush bloomed beside the front gate.
The sweet scent of lilac filled the spring air.

definition: an uncertain situation in which you are waiting and cannot act

collocations.example: The project has been in limbo since the funding stopped.
The long delay left her career in a state of limbo.

definition: the center of public attention and interest

collocations.example: The young actor suddenly found himself in the limelight.
She loves to steal the limelight at every event.

definition: a fat or similar substance found in living things and in food

collocations.example: The doctor checked his blood lipid levels at the clinic.
A healthy diet helps control blood lipids.

definition: a long, boring list of things, especially complaints

collocations.example: She listed a long litany of complaints about her job.
He recited a litany of excuses for being late again.

definition: a print made using a specially prepared flat stone or metal plate

collocations.example: The gallery sold an original lithograph by the famous artist.
He bought a lithograph of the old harbor.

definition: a special uniform worn by servants or staff of a company

collocations.example: The servants were all dressed in fine livery.
The driver wore the company's distinctive green livery.

definition: to throw or hit something so that it moves in a high, gentle curve

collocations.example: She lobbed the ball high over her opponent's head.
He lobbed the keys across the room to me.

definition: a place where something happens or is set

collocations.example: The beach was the perfect locale for the wedding.
The small town is a popular locale for film shoots.

definition: (British, informal) a toilet

collocations.example: Can I use your loo before we leave?
She got up to go to the loo during the break.

definition: traditional knowledge, beliefs, or stories about a subject

collocations.example: The guide shared the ancient lore of the mountains.
According to local lore, a ghost haunts the old inn.

definition: a small insect that lives on the skin or hair of people and animals

collocations.example: A head louse can spread quickly among schoolchildren.
The vet checked the dog carefully for a single louse.

definition: to put oil or grease on something so that it moves smoothly

collocations.example: Mineral oil is used to lubricate the machinery.
Remember to lubricate the moving parts regularly.

definition: only slightly warm, often less warm than you would like

collocations.example: Wash the wound gently with clean lukewarm water.
She frowned at her lukewarm coffee and pushed it away.

definition: described in shocking detail, especially about violence or scandal

collocations.example: The newspaper printed all the lurid details of the crime.
He told a lurid tale of his wild travels abroad.

definition: a clear fluid in the body that helps fight infection

collocations.example: The doctor felt the swollen lymph nodes in his neck.
Lymph fluid carries white blood cells around the body.

definition: a type of cancer that affects the body's lymph system

collocations.example: He was diagnosed with lymphoma last spring.
Doctors used chemotherapy to treat the lymphoma.

definition: a rich and powerful person in business or industry

collocations.example: The oil magnate owned several luxury homes abroad.
She became a powerful business magnate within a decade.

definition: a tree or shrub with large white or pink sweet-smelling flowers

collocations.example: A magnolia tree bloomed in the front yard.
The large magnolia flowers gave off a sweet scent.

definition: to injure someone so badly that part of their body is permanently damaged

collocations.example: Land mines can maim and kill innocent civilians.
The accident seriously maimed several of the passengers.

definition: the most important part of something that provides support

collocations.example: Cocoa is the economic mainstay of the region.
Volunteers are the mainstay of the small charity.

definition: wanting to harm others; showing an evil intention

collocations.example: She gave him a cold, malevolent stare.
The story is about a malevolent spirit in the old house.

definition: a failure of a machine or part to work correctly

collocations.example: A computer malfunction delayed all the flights.
Engineers found a malfunction in the cooling system.

definition: poor health caused by not having enough food or the right kind of food

collocations.example: Many children in the region suffer from malnutrition.
The rescued refugees showed signs of severe malnutrition.

definition: the long thick hair on the neck of a horse or lion

collocations.example: She gently brushed the horse's mane before the ride.
The male lion's mane was thick and golden.

definition: to damage something badly by crushing or twisting it

collocations.example: The crash mangled the car almost beyond recognition.
His bike was badly mangled by the passing truck.

definition: an extremely strong desire or enthusiasm for something

collocations.example: He has a mania for collecting old foreign coins.
Football mania swept across the whole country that summer.

definition: a harbor where small boats and yachts are kept

collocations.example: They docked the yacht at the marina for the night.
Dozens of sailboats were moored in the marina.

definition: an alcoholic cocktail made with gin or vodka and vermouth

collocations.example: He ordered a dry martini at the hotel bar.
She carefully mixed a martini for her guest.

definition: a cosmetic used to darken and thicken the eyelashes

collocations.example: She prefers waterproof mascara for rainy days.
He watched her apply mascara before the party.

definition: a person whose job is to build or work with stone or brick

collocations.example: A skilled stone mason repaired the old church wall.
Skilled masons laid bricks for the new wall all day.

definition: the state of being married; marriage

collocations.example: The couple were joined together in holy matrimony.
They entered into matrimony after a long courtship.
